KR.read: Korea's fragrances segment now has domestic size and production data, not just exports, though the aggregator readings disagree sharply. Two LOW-confidence RETAIL 'perfume' market-size figures for the identical year 2025 conflict: IMARC US$792.5mn versus Expert Market Research US$485.19mn, a 1.63x gap that scope alone does not explain (EMR's stated scope, 'fragrances and perfume', is wider than IMARC's 'perfume', yet EMR's number is smaller) - neither is a headline figure without a Euromonitor or MFDS/KOSIS cross-check. A HIGH-confidence MFDS PRODUCTION figure also exists: KRW 68.0bn (2024, ~US$46.0mn) for the '방향용' (fragrance) cosmetics-registered product type - about 17x smaller than IMARC's retail figure, which reflects both the basis difference (factory-gate vs retail) and that MFDS excludes imported fragrance in an import-dominated Korean market, not a conflict to reconcile. Export figures (US$0.06bn 2025 EXPORT_FOB HIGH; US$0.039471bn 2024 world HS3303 HIGH) are unchanged, with a negligible [CORRIDOR]-tagged US$6,000 flow to India in 2024.
KR.trend: A PRODUCTION-basis growth figure now exists: +14.67% YoY for 2024 (ESTIMATE confidence, derived from two adjacent years in the same MFDS annex table) - domestic manufacturing growth only, excluding imports, and notably slower than the +20.9% all-cosmetics production growth over the same period. Three forecast CAGRs disagree on both level and pace: IMARC 4.62% (2026-2034, LOW), Expert Market Research 6.30% (2026-2035, LOW, ~36% faster than IMARC), and SPER Market Research 5.2% (2023-2028, LOW) - a roughly 2.5x dispersion in the underlying market-size levels these three aggregators imply, which is why no single Korea fragrance market size is presented as a headline figure. The export-side +46.2% YoY note for 2025 (HIGH confidence) remains the most reliable growth signal, though it describes trade flow, not domestic demand.
KR.caveats: SPER's page contains an internally impossible trajectory (a stated 2022 level and 2033 endpoint inconsistent with its own claimed CAGR) - only its CAGR is recorded, not its size figures. The two RETAIL market-size aggregators disagree 1.63x with no scope explanation, and the MFDS production figure measures a different, narrower, domestic-only base - none of the three should be combined or averaged.

IN.read: India fragrances has two RETAIL market-size estimates, both LOW confidence: US$2.6bn (2024) covering perfume plus deodorant combined, and a narrower US$0.281bn (FY24) covering perfume only - different scope, so not directly comparable to each other. Import data is HIGH confidence: India imported US$0.331681bn of fragrances (HS 3303) from the world in 2024, with Korea (US$0.000135bn, [CORRIDOR]-tagged) and China (US$0.000249bn) each a minor source. An ESTIMATE-confidence import-dependence figure of 12.8% notes that premium fragrance is import-reliant (UAE the largest source, then France) while mass-market perfume/deodorant is largely made domestically. A HIGH-confidence company figure now exists alongside these: Titan Company's Fragrances division (SKINN and Fastrack Perfumes brands) grew approximately 26% YoY in Q4FY25 (NET_REALISATION basis, BSE/NSE regulatory filing) - company-level, not a category-wide market figure, and Titan does not separately disclose Fragrances' absolute revenue. The Vini Cosmetics/Fogg company figure (FY25 revenue INR 1200cr, NET_REALISATION, MEDIUM confidence) reflects one company's deodorant business, not the fragrances segment as a whole.
IN.trend: Formal forecast CAGRs now exist alongside the informal figures embedded in the market-size notes. On the perfume-only scope (the closest match to the taxonomy segment): IMARC 5.36% (2026-2034, LOW). On the wider perfume-plus-deodorant scope: IMARC 10.26% (2026-2034, LOW) and TechSci 11.54% (2025-2030, LOW) on differing size bases roughly 1.9x apart - deodorants roughly double both the base and the growth rate, so the perfume-only and perfume-plus-deodorant readings are not substitutes for each other. The market-size claims' own notes separately carry two older, informal CAGRs (roughly 11.1% for the perfume+deodorant estimate, 15.23% for the perfume-only estimate) that predate these formal IMARC/TechSci figures and are not independently corroborated forecasts in their own right. Titan's ~26% Q4FY25 figure is the only observed year-on-year read, and it is company-level, not a category rate.
IN.caveats: Five different growth-rate readings now exist for India fragrances across two scope definitions (perfume-only vs perfume-plus-deodorant) and should not be blended into one number. The 12.8% import-dependence figure is itself labelled ESTIMATE/derived rather than a directly sourced number. Titan's growth figure reflects one company's two-brand division within a larger 'Emerging Businesses' segment, not the category.

combined.read: A like-for-like comparison of Korea and India fragrances remains difficult even with fuller data on both sides: Korea's RETAIL market-size aggregators disagree 1.63x (US$792.5mn vs US$485.19mn, both 2025) and India's disagree by scope (US$2.6bn perfume+deodorant vs US$0.281bn perfume-only), so neither geography has one settled value_usd_bn to set against the other. The Korea-to-India corridor trade flow is present but tiny on both sides of the ledger (KR exports to India US$6,000 in 2024; India imports from Korea US$135,000 in 2024, both [CORRIDOR]-tagged), suggesting fragrances remains a minor thread of the broader K-beauty corridor relative to categories like skincare.
